## Objectives {.objective-slide}

:::: columns
::: {.column width="90%"}

- Evaluate the composition and risk distribution of the motor insurance portfolio

- Analyse claim behaviour and underwriting profitability patterns

- Identify high-risk customer and vehicle segments associated with higher claim exposure

- Support data-driven pricing, underwriting, and portfolio management decisions through visual analytics

:::
::::

::: notes
This study applies the IDEA framework to evaluate the motor insurance portfolio from both risk and profitability perspectives. The analysis focuses on identifying claim behaviour patterns, underwriting profitability dynamics, and high-risk customer and vehicle segments that may contribute to portfolio volatility.

Using exploratory visual analytics techniques, the study examines relationships across policy, customer, vehicle, and claim-related variables to uncover meaningful risk patterns and profitability insights.

The findings aim to support more informed pricing, underwriting, and portfolio management decisions while demonstrating the value of visual analytics in insurance portfolio analysis.
:::

## Portfolio Overview

### Dataset Summary

-   Years Covered: 2022–2024

-   Total Policy Records: 354,140

-   Policy-level motor insurance portfolio

-   Customer, vehicle, claims, and financial variables analysed

### Key Areas of Analysis

-   Claim behaviour patterns

-   Underwriting profitability

-   High-risk customer segments

-   Vehicle risk exposure

-   Pricing adequacy evaluation

::: notes
This slide provides a high-level overview of the motor insurance portfolio dataset used in the analysis. The dataset contains more than 350,000 policy-level records collected between 2022 and 2024, covering customer, vehicle, claims, and financial-related variables.

The analysis focuses on understanding portfolio composition, claim behaviour, underwriting profitability, and identifying high-risk customer segments. Particular attention is given to pricing adequacy and vehicle-related risk exposure, which are important factors affecting insurance profitability and portfolio sustainability.
:::

::::::: smaller-bullets

<h4 style="text-align:center;">

Claim Status Composition

-   85.7% of policies did not report claims

<h4 style="text-align:center;">

Premium Distribution

</h4>

:::
::::::
:::::::

::: notes
This slide provides an overview of the portfolio structure and overall claim concentration. The claim status distribution shows that most policies remain claim-free, while claims are concentrated within a smaller proportion of policyholders. The premium distribution further highlights strong right-skewness, where most policies are concentrated within lower-to-moderate premium ranges alongside a smaller segment of high-premium policies. These findings indicate varying customer risk profiles and provide context for the subsequent analysis on profitability, underwriting performance, and high-risk portfolio segments.
:::

## Claim Behaviour Analysis

::::::: smaller-bullets
:::::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
![](images/Yearly%20Portfolio%20Performance.png){width="100%" height="260px"}

<h4 style="text-align:center;">

Yearly Portfolio Performance

</h4>

-   Portfolio claim indicators increased progressively from 2022 to 2024

-   Loss ratio and underpricing exposure intensified over time, signalling growing profitability pressure

-   Rising claim frequency contributed to deteriorating underwriting performance across the portfolio
:::

::: {.column width="4%"}
 
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
![](images/Claim%20Severity%20Behaviour.png){width="100%" height="260px"}

<h4 style="text-align:center;">

Claim Severity Distribution

</h4>

-   Higher vehicle value segments demonstrate broader claim severity distributions and stronger tail-risk behaviour

-   Extreme incurred-loss observations are more concentrated among premium vehicle categories

-   Uneven claim severity patterns suggest differing levels of financial exposure across insured vehicle segments
:::
::::::
:::::::

::: notes
This slide examines claim behaviour and underwriting risk patterns within the motor insurance portfolio. The yearly portfolio performance chart indicates that claim frequency, loss ratio, and underpricing exposure increased steadily from 2022 to 2024, reflecting worsening underwriting conditions over time. The claim severity distribution further reveals that higher-value vehicle segments exhibit broader loss distributions and stronger tail-risk exposure, indicating greater financial volatility. Together, these findings suggest that portfolio profitability pressure is influenced by both worsening claim trends over time and concentrated high-severity losses among selected vehicle segments.
:::

The age composition chart shows that portfolio exposure is concentrated among middle-aged drivers, especially those aged 40 to 59, while younger drivers form a relatively small share of the portfolio. These findings suggest that although the portfolio is largely made up of mature and experienced drivers, customer risk should still be assessed together with claim behaviour, vehicle characteristics, and policy type.

Together, these findings suggest that product design, coverage structure, and underwriting strategy play an important role in portfolio profitability and long-term sustainability.
:::

## High-Risk Segment Analysis

::::::: smaller-bullets
:::::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
![](images/Driver%20Age%20Influence%20Claim%20Risk.png){width="100%" height="250px"}

<h4 style="text-align:center;">

Driver Age and Policy Risk Interaction

</h4>

-   Claim risk varies across both driver age groups and policy products

-   Younger drivers exhibit higher claim exposure across several policy types

-   Comprehensive products remain higher-risk even across different age groups
:::

::: {.column width="4%"}
 
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
![](images/Policy%20Product%20Tail-Risk%20Exposure.png){width="100%" height="250px"}

<h4 style="text-align:center;">

Policy Product Tail-Risk Exposure

</h4>

-   Comprehensive policies show wider claim severity distributions

-   Certain policy products exhibit greater exposure to extreme claim events

-   Policy type remains an important segmentation factor for underwriting risk
:::
::::::
:::::::

::: notes
This slide examines higher-risk portfolio segments from both customer and product perspectives. The driver age interaction analysis shows that claim exposure differs across age groups and policy products, with younger drivers generally demonstrating higher claim risk across several insurance categories. Comprehensive products consistently remain associated with higher underwriting exposure regardless of driver age profile.

The policy product tail-risk analysis further highlights that certain insurance products exhibit broader claim severity distributions and greater exposure to extreme loss events. These findings suggest that underwriting risk is influenced not only by customer demographics but also by product structure and claim severity behaviour. Together, the analyses support the importance of risk-based segmentation and targeted underwriting strategies to improve portfolio sustainability and pricing adequacy.
:::

## Key Insights

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="34%"}
<br>

![](images/Key%20Insights-01.png){fig-align="center"}
:::

:::: {.column width="66%"}
### Insights {.smaller-heading}

::: smaller-bullets
-   Most policies did not report claims, suggesting that portfolio risk exposure is concentrated within a smaller subset of policyholders

-   Comprehensive insurance products consistently demonstrated higher claim frequency, claim severity, loss ratios, and underpricing pressure

-   Claim behaviour and underwriting profitability varied substantially across policy structures and customer segments

-   Premium adequacy alone does not fully determine profitability, as higher-premium products may still experience elevated claim costs

-   Vehicle characteristics, pricing structure, and customer risk exposure jointly contribute to underwriting volatility and portfolio sustainability
:::
::::
::::::

::: notes
This section summarizes the major findings derived from the exploratory visual analytics conducted on the motor insurance portfolio dataset.

The analysis revealed that although most policyholders did not submit claims, profitability pressure is concentrated within a smaller high-risk segment of the portfolio.

Comprehensive insurance products consistently displayed higher claim frequency, higher claim severity, and greater underpricing pressure compared to other policy types.

The findings also demonstrate that premium adequacy alone does not guarantee underwriting profitability, as certain high-premium products continue to experience elevated claim costs and financial pressure.

Overall, portfolio profitability appears to be influenced by the combined interaction of customer risk exposure, policy structure, vehicle characteristics, and claim behaviour dynamics.
:::

## Conclusion & Future Work

![](images/Conclusion+FutureWork.png){width="48%"}

</div>

:::::::::: columns

::::: {.column width="55%"}

### Conclusion {.smaller-subheading}

::: {.smaller-bullets}

- Motor insurance profitability is shaped by claim behaviour, pricing adequacy, policy structure, and vehicle risk exposure

- Comprehensive products consistently showed higher claim severity, loss ratios, and underpricing pressure

- Visual analytics revealed meaningful patterns in underwriting profitability, portfolio volatility, and risk concentration

:::

:::::

::::: {.column width="45%"}

### Future Work {.smaller-subheading}

::: {.smaller-bullets}

- Extend the analysis using additional behavioural and operational variables such as telematics and fraud indicators

- Perform confirmatory statistical analysis to validate the exploratory findings

- Expand longitudinal analysis to monitor evolving underwriting and profitability trends

:::

:::::

::::::::::

::: notes
This final slide summarizes the overall conclusions and future analytical opportunities.

The study shows that motor insurance profitability is influenced by multiple interacting factors, including claim behaviour, pricing adequacy, policy structure, and vehicle risk exposure.

Comprehensive insurance products consistently demonstrated higher claim severity, higher loss ratios, and stronger underpricing pressure.

The analysis also highlights how visual analytics can support deeper understanding of underwriting profitability, portfolio volatility, and emerging risk concentration patterns.

Future work could extend the analysis using additional behavioural and operational variables such as telematics, fraud indicators, and longer-term underwriting trends.
:::
